trident-hey-jude: Trident Studios was a British recording facility, located at 17 St Anne's Court in London's Soho district between 1968 and 1981.
While Abbey Road Studios still used only four-track at the time, Trident's Ampex eight-track machine drew the Beatles on 31 July 1968 to record their song "Hey Jude".
hendrix-ronnie-scotts: Ronnie Scott's Jazz Club is a jazz club that has operated in Soho, London, since 1959.
In 1965 it moved to a larger venue nearby at 47 Frith Street.
Jimi Hendrix's last public performance was at Ronnie Scott's, in 1970.
carnaby-time: Bands such as the Small Faces, the Who and the Rolling Stones appeared in the area, to work ..., to shop and to socialise, so it became one of the coolest destinations associated with 1960s Swinging London.

The Carnaby Street contingent of Swinging London stormed into North American and international awareness with the 15 April 1966 publication of Time magazine's cover story that extolled this street's role
markov-umbrella: Georgi Ivanov Markov (1 March 1929 – 11 September 1978) was a Bulgarian dissident writer.
On 7 September 1978, Markov walked across Waterloo Bridge spanning the River Thames and waited to take a bus to his job at the BBC.

Markov was assassinated by being injected with a tiny pellet containing poison, possibly ricin, which was covertly delivered into his leg on a London street by an unknown man who used an umbrella as a weapon.
Georgi Markov, a Bulgarian dissident, was assassinated on Waterloo Bridge on 7 September 1978 by agents of the Bulgarian secret police (Wikipedia: Waterloo Bridge)
blind-beggar: The Blind Beggar is a pub in Whitechapel Road in the East End of London, England, at the junction with Cambridge Heath Road.
It is where Ronnie Kray murdered George Cornell in front of witnesses.
On 9 March 1966, Ronnie Kray shot and murdered George Cornell, an associate of a rival gang, the Richardsons, as he was sitting at the bar.
The Blind Beggar is notorious for its connection to East End gangsters the Kray twins.
spaghetti-house-siege: The Spaghetti House siege took place between 28 September and 3 October 1975.
An attempted robbery of the Spaghetti House restaurant in Knightsbridge, London, went wrong and the police were quickly on the scene.
They released all the hostages unharmed after six days.
biba-kensington: The store moved to the seven-storey Derry & Toms department store on Kensington High Street, which immediately attracted up to a million customers weekly, making it one of the most visited tourist attractions in London.
In 1973, Dorothy Perkins was bought by British Land ... (Big Biba section)
withnail-west-house: In the 1987 film Withnail and I (portrayed by Richard E. Grant and Paul McGann), the house is Withnail's flamboyantly gay Uncle Monty (Richard Griffiths)' London home.
punk-100-club: The 100 Club Punk Special ... was a two-day event held at the 100 Club venue in Oxford Street, London, England, on 20 and 21 September 1976.
concert promoter Ron Watts approached Malcolm McLaren, manager of the Sex Pistols, ... and proposed that they headline the event.
Line-up: Subway Sect, Siouxsie and the Banshees, The Clash, Sex Pistols; Stinky Toys, Chris Spedding & the Vibrators, The Damned, Buzzcocks
live-aid-wembley: It later played host to a number of concerts and events, most notably the British leg of Live Aid, which featured such acts as David Bowie, Queen, Paul McCartney, Elton John, Phil Collins, Status Quo, the Who, Dire Straits and U2, held at the stadium on 13 July 1985.
clockwork-thamesmead: The Tavy Bridge area of Thamesmead South, including Southmere Lake, was used as a setting for the Stanley Kubrick film A Clockwork Orange (1971).
The pre-1974 parts of Thamesmead are a mix of modernist town houses, medium-rise and 12-storey blocks system built in concrete, which have featured in various films due to their 'rough urban look'
